name: COPD (European Calibration)
remarks: SYNTHEA MODULE: COPD — European Epidemiology Edition
Calibrated against:
- ERS White Book 2013; ERS update 2022
- BOLD Europe study (Buist et al. Lancet 2007)
- GOLD 2023 COPD Guidelines
- GBD 2019: Europe-specific COPD burden
- Eurostat EHIS Wave 3 (2019)
- WHO Europe NCD Report 2022
Key calibration changes vs US default module:
- Module was effectively absent in default output — fully rebuilt
- Overall prevalence ~6.5% of adults (BOLD Europe)
- Strong post-50 age weighting (BOLD shows <2% under 50, 10%+ over 60)
- Smoking as primary risk factor (prevalence ~25% EU adults — WHO 2022)
- GOLD staging: GOLD 1-4 distribution from BOLD Europe study
- Medication: GOLD preferred A/B/E pathway (LAMA/ICS-LABA/triple)
- Exacerbation rates from ECLIPSE / TORCH studies
European age-stratified prevalence (BOLD Europe / GBD 2019):
PATCH (calibration round 2):
Reduced all COPD onset rates by 30%. Previous calibration produced
~18% cohort prevalence; target ~12-13% (BOLD Europe).

R4 verification round 2 (2026-08-29): rates x3.2. The R4 run measured 2.01% period prevalence against a 6.5% ERS/BOLD reference (-69%). Note this module was edited 2026-07-29, two days after the R3 output was generated, so R3's COPD figure never reflected this code.
RECALIBRATION 2026-09-30 — rates derived from this module's own band targets.
The x3.2 applied in R4 verification round 2 was fitted against CRUDE cohort
prevalence, which understates age-dependent conditions on a cohort whose mean
age is 41. Age-standardised to the EU27 adult structure the module measured
7.6% against the 6.5% row reference (+18%), and +35% against the 2.5/6/10.5/
14/15% band targets in the remarks above.
Both tiers are now fitted so that the 25/75 mixture, averaged over each band's
age range, equals that band's BOLD Europe target. The base-risk loop was
re-banded from three bands to the high-risk loop's five so a common fit was
possible; base risk is held at high risk / 10.
Predicted EU27-adult standardised prevalence: 5.7% (was 7.7%).
KNOWN ARTEFACT: the fitted rates are NOT monotonic in age (1.455 / 0.985 /
2.354 / 0.794 / 0.095 %/yr). Real COPD incidence does not fall after 70. The
cause is that this module has no disease-specific excess mortality - measured,
COPD carries 10.2% mortality against an 8.8% cohort baseline, while real COPD
carries substantial excess mortality. Real prevalence plateaus in old age
because affected people die sooner; a model that keeps them alive can only hold
the plateau by almost ceasing to generate new cases. Adding excess mortality
would let incidence stay plausible AND hold the prevalence curve - the better
fix, deferred because it is a structural change.
NOTE ON THE REFERENCES: the band targets imply 5.7% EU27-adult standardised,
the validation table's row says 6.5% - a 12% disagreement between two figures
that both cite BOLD Europe. The bands are the more specific source and were
followed.
COPD is extremely rare before 40. BOLD study finds negligible prevalence <40.
Smoking prevalence in Europe ~25% (WHO Europe 2022).
COPD risk: ~25% of smokers develop COPD (BOLD study).
Non-smokers can develop COPD via biomass, occupational exposure (~15% of cases).
Routes: high-risk (smokers) vs base-risk (non-smokers).
Tier is assigned once to an attribute. The annual delay routes on that attribute so a patient does not change smoking status between years.

GOLD 1: Mild COPD. FEV1 >=80% predicted. SNOMED 13645005.
GOLD 2: Moderate COPD. FEV1 50-79% predicted.
GOLD 3: Severe COPD. FEV1 30-49% predicted.
FEV1/FVC ratio <0.70 required for GOLD diagnosis (post-bronchodilator). LOINC 19926-5.
GOLD 2023: smoking cessation is the single most effective intervention for COPD.
GOLD 2023 Pharmacological Treatment:
Group A (low symptoms, low risk): SAMA or SABA prn
Group B (more symptoms, low risk): LAMA preferred
Group E (high risk exacerbation): LAMA + LABA; add ICS if eos >=300
Distribution: ~30% SABA, ~40% LAMA, ~30% triple (ICS+LABA+LAMA)
Salbutamol (albuterol) 100mcg MDI — GOLD Group A. RxNorm 745679.
